faq.q: Is December a good time for a yacht charter in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes. December offers mild weather (16–18°C), 8 hours of sunshine, and calm seas – perfect for a festive cruise along the Costa del Sol. You avoid summer crowds and enjoy lower rates.

faq.q: What is the sea temperature in Marbella in December?
faq.a: The Mediterranean sea temperature in December averages 16–17°C. While swimming is brisk, it's fine for a quick dip or enjoying the deck. Many guests prefer soaking up the sun and sipping cava.

faq.q: Which yacht is best for a December 2027 charter?
faq.a: For a group up to 12, the Mangusta 80 (24m) is ideal – it includes a free jet ski and has a spacious flybridge. For smaller groups, the Azimut 39 (11 pax) or Astondoa 40 (9 pax) are cost-effective options.

faq.q: What is included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs.

faq.q: Can we celebrate New Year's Eve on a yacht?
faq.a: Absolutely. Many guests book a sunset cruise on 31 December. With sunset around 18:00, you can watch the fireworks over Puerto Banús. Contact us via WhatsApp for availability and custom packages.

faq.q: What are the wind and sea conditions like in December?
faq.a: Winds are typically light (5–10 knots) from the west or northwest, producing calm seas with wave heights under 0.5m. This makes for stable cruising along the coast from Marbella to Estepona.

faq.q: How long do daylight hours last in December?
faq.a: Daylight runs from about 08:30 to 18:00, giving you roughly 9.5 hours of daylight with 8 hours of direct sun. Afternoon charters (13:00–18:00) are popular for catching the golden hour.

faq.q: What should I wear for a December yacht charter?
faq.a: Bring layers: a light jumper or fleece, a windproof jacket, and comfortable shoes. Sunglasses and sunscreen are still needed due to UV reflection off the water. A hat is useful for the breeze.

data.body_html:
December 2027 yacht charters in Marbella offer a unique winter escape: mild 16–18°C air temperatures, 8 hours of daily sunshine, and calm Mediterranean seas. Unlike the summer rush, you'll enjoy a relaxed atmosphere from Puerto Banús, with festive touches like cava and white wine included on every booking. Whether you're planning a Christmas celebration or a New Year's Eve cruise, our fleet of 18 boats – from the compact Dubhe (5 pax) to the 29m Ferretti 94 – is ready for you. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and Spanish VAT (21%). See our full fleet overview for details.

December Weather in Marbella: What to Expect

Marbella enjoys a microclimate that keeps winter mild. Average highs reach 18°C in December, with lows around 13°C. The sea temperature hovers at 16–17°C – refreshing but not freezing. Rainfall is low (about 60mm for the month, spread over 6–7 days), and you can expect 8 hours of direct sun daily. Winds are gentle (5–10 knots from the west or northwest), creating calm seas with waves under 0.5m. For a detailed forecast, check the Marbella yacht charter weather December 2027 page.

Best Yachts for a Winter Cruise

Our fleet includes options for every group size. For a festive gathering of up to 12 guests, the Mangusta 80 (24m) is a top choice – it includes a free jet ski on 4-hour+ bookings, adding a thrill to your winter cruise. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offers enclosed saloons for cooler days. Smaller groups can opt for the Tier A boats: Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax), priced from €749 for 2 hours to €2,299 for 8 hours. All depart from Puerto Banús. Browse our full fleet for more options.

Festive Cruises: Christmas & New Year's Eve

December is perfect for a themed cruise. Many guests book a sunset trip (13:00–18:00) to toast the season with cava and white wine, both included. For New Year's Eve, you can watch the fireworks over Puerto Banús from the water – a memory that beats any restaurant table. Contact us via WhatsApp to arrange a custom package, including decorations or a private chef. All charters include light snacks, beer, and soft drinks.

Where to Cruise in December

From Puerto Banús, popular routes include a coastal cruise to Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, where you can anchor for a quiet swim. Alternatively, head west to Estepona (about 10 NM) or east to Cabopino (8 NM). The calm seas make longer trips to Sotogrande (25 NM) feasible on larger yachts like the Ferretti 94. Keep an eye on the sunset – it's around 18:00, so plan your return accordingly.

Pricing & Booking Details

Our pricing is transparent. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) cost €749 for 2 hours, €1,199 for 4 hours, €1,799 for 6 hours, and €2,299 for 8 hours. The Mangusta 80 (white or grey) starts at €4,719 for a minimum 4 hours and includes a free jet ski. For all other boats – including the Azimut 58, Ferretti 94, and Lagoon 380 – pricing is on request via WhatsApp. Every booking includes skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT. No surprises. For a quick overview, see our pricing page.

What to Bring for a December Charter

Layers are key: a light fleece or jumper, a windproof jacket, and non-slip shoes. Sunglasses and sunscreen are still essential – UV reflection off the water is strong even in winter. A hat helps against the breeze. If you plan to swim, a wetsuit (3mm) makes the 16°C water comfortable. We provide towels and safety equipment.
